reason: History held to 50 persistence calls/s. The key is history.persistenceMaxQPS, default 9000, per history host (common/dynamicconfig/constants.go:1549-1553). History reads it as a function (service/history/configs/config.go:440) for its persistence client's host limiter (service/history/fx.go:290-326; common/persistence/client/fx.go:115-161, quotas.go:63-95) and, at 30%, for its queue readers (service/history/transfer_queue_factory.go:73-80, queue_factory_base.go:217-234; history.transferProcessorMaxPollHostRPS is 0, constants.go:1977-1979). The namespace and per-shard namespace limiters read it too: history.persistenceNamespaceMaxQPS and history.persistencePerShardNamespaceMaxQPS default to 0, and 0 falls back to the host value (constants.go:1559-1574; common/persistence/client/quotas.go:131-155, 164-193; service/history/configs/config.go:442-444). A call is checked against the per-shard limiter, then the namespace one, then the host one (common/persistence/persistence_rate_limited_clients.go:1165-1173). Per shard, namespace default's calls stay far under 50/s on 512 shards; for the namespace as a whole they do not, so a call for namespace default is refused first by the namespace limiter, with ResourceExhausted "Namespace Persistence Max QPS Reached." (scope NAMESPACE, persistence_rate_limited_clients.go:29-33), which IsServiceClientTransientError does not count as transient (common/util.go:312-325). A call with no namespace meets the host limiter, "System Persistence Max QPS Reached." (lines 24-28). It takes effect without a restart: the file client swaps in the new values on its next poll of a file with a newer mtime (common/dynamicconfig/file_based_client.go:134-147, 172, 195), and each limiter reads its rate again on the first call after its 1-minute timer (common/quotas/dynamic_rate_limiter_impl.go:9, 68-76, 130-139). The limiters exist because the value was above 0 at start (common/persistence/client/fx.go:119); the health-aware limiter beside them is off by default and allows everything (common/dynamicconfig/shared_constants.go:82-83, common/persistence/client/health_request_rate_limiter.go:71-77).

reason: A reach probe: a change the matching client's README says is harmful, which the source says laug at 20/s does not see. Read partitions cut to 1 while write partitions stay at 4, the order the README warns against: "when reducing, write partitions has to be reduced first, and then the extra partitions have to be empty before reducing read partitions" (client/matching/README.md:69-70). Both default to 4 (common/dynamicconfig/constants.go:1222-1231, shared_constants.go:9 and 48-50), and laug.yaml sets both to 4 for namespace default. Frontends route each poll by the read count and history routes each task by the write count, both read on every call (client/matching/loadbalancer.go:68-69, 76-90, 94-113; client.go:184-206), so the change takes effect on each role's next file poll, with no limiter in between. Listed as BLOCK until 2026-10-14, when a review of this prediction found it predicts ADVANCE.
prediction: Tasks do not strand: they reach pollers by forwarding, and the verdict should ADVANCE. Writes stay uniform over 4 partitions (loadbalancer.go:88-89) and every poll goes to partition 0, the parent of partitions 1 to 3 (common/tqid/task_queue_id.go:324-332, with matching.forwarderMaxChildrenPerNode 20, constants.go:1271-1275). Every non-root partition runs a task forwarder to its parent for sync-match offers and its database backlog alike (service/matching/pri_matcher.go:136-140, 166-248; the priority matcher is the default, matching.useNewMatcher, constants.go:1414-1419), at most matching.forwarderMaxRatePerSecond 10/s with 1 forward in flight (constants.go:1261-1270, pri_matcher.go:126). A backlog task forwarded to the root waits there for a poller up to matching.backlogTaskForwardTimeout 60 s (constants.go:1436-1440, pri_matcher.go:412-422). At 20/s, partitions 1 to 3 each get about 5 workflow tasks/s and 5 activity tasks/s, half the cap (activity eager execution is off, constants.go:193-197; the Go SDK sends the second workflow task to its sticky queue, verify). Forwarding is not new: the healthy baseline already forwarded about 7.5 sync-match misses/s (447 Canceled in 60 s, load/steady-state.yaml), and with every poller at the root a forwarded task is more likely to find one waiting. Above 40/s the 3 forwarders (30/s for 3/4 of the tasks) saturate, backlog on partitions 1 to 3 grows, and the sweep should find workflows Running; laug does not load a cell that hard. A BLOCK at 20/s, on schedule-to-start, would show the forwarders cost more than the source says.
